title: Latency & Throughput Discovery — Silverpine AI
summary: High-level discovery focused on p95 latency targets for streaming chat, steady-state throughput and burst behavior. Customer comparing Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) for productionizing an agent product with multimodal prompts. Key constraints: p95 <= 200ms for short chat replies, occasional 2k token completions, 800 concurrent sessions at peak, strict SOC2 and KMS requirements.
topics: p95 latency targets and example SLAs
concurrency and burst sizing (800 concurrent peak)
hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs
security/compliance (SOC 2, KMS, audit logs, VPC peering)
transcript:
[00:00:00] Samir (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — this is Samir from Redwood. Jin from our SE team is on as well. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:08] Mira (CTO): Doing well, thanks. We have about 45 minutes set aside to go deep on latency and throughput — trying to decide hosting mode.
[00:00:15] Samir (AE): Great. Quick agenda: understand your p95 targets, concurrency patterns, streaming needs, and then Jin will talk about benchmarks and capacity sizing.
[00:00:25] Tom (SRE): Quick context — we run a conversational agent for e-commerce search, typical turn is 40-120 tokens but sometimes we have long summarizations up to 2k tokens. Peak concurrency around 700–900 sessions, sustained 300.
[00:00:37] Jin (SE): Okay that helps. When you say p95 target, are you aiming at response start (first token) or full completion p95? Those are very different.
[00:00:44] Leah (ML Eng): Primarily first token for user-perceived latency, so streaming start matters. Full completion can be higher.
[00:00:51] Samir (AE): Noted. Typical goal we've seen is p95 under 200ms for first token on 32–128 token responses. Is that in line with you?
[00:00:58] Mira (CTO): Yes, ideally <=200ms at p95 for short replies. For longer completions we'd accept higher but start needs to be fast.
[00:01:05] Jin (SE): Short replies at p95 ~200ms — on hosted that's usually achievable on modern open models with optimized kernels and streaming. We'll ask about sequence length distribution, since KV cache warmups and prefix caching matter.
[00:01:14] Tom (SRE): About KV cache — we have lots of repeated prompts and system prefixes so caching would help. How does Redwood's prefix/KV caching work across hosted vs dedicated?
[00:01:22] Jin (SE): We do automatic prefix caching where compatible. On Dedicated you can pin instances and get warmer caches persistently; on hosted it's multi-tenant so cache locality varies, but we use smart routing to try to preserve affinity for hot keys. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full isolation and predictable cache hit rates.
[00:01:34] Mira (CTO): For cost, we prefer hosted if it meets targets, but if we need guaranteed p95 and consistent throughput maybe Dedicated. We also have compliance: SOC2 and customer data must be encrypted with our KMS.
[00:01:43] Samir (AE): We support KMS integrations with both Dedicated and Private. Hosted can use Redwood-managed keys or BYOK for enterprise — there are details in our security pack. We'll share that.
[00:01:52] Tom (SRE): On concurrency, what's the recommended batch sizing and how it impacts p95? We saw a vendor batch to 32 which spiked p95.
[00:02:00] Jin (SE): Right — batching increases throughput but can add latency depending on batching windows. Redwood's runtime uses continuous batching and workload-aware policies: we avoid adding artificial batching delay for low-latency routes, you can set latency SLO per route. For example, route A: p95 <=200ms, we prioritize single-request scheduling and micro-batching.
[00:02:15] [00:02:15] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[00:02:18] Jin (SE): For token/sec benchmarks — we typically measure both tokens/sec per-GPU and end-to-end token/sec observed for workloads. For streaming start latency we measure 'first-byte' p95 and then steady-state throughput for long completions.
[00:02:30] Mira (CTO): Can you share an example benchmark? Say for a 13B quantized int8 model, 128 token reply, hosted vs dedicated difference?
[00:02:39] Jin (SE): Rough numbers — on hosted across our catalog a 13B int8 model first-token p95 might be ~120–180ms under light load; under heavy concurrent load that can drift depending on multi-tenant pressure. On Dedicated with pinned GPUs and optimized kernel selection we see tighter p95 bounds — e.g., 90–140ms. But exact depends on seq len, batch policy, and caching.
[00:02:58] Tom (SRE): What's the approach for burst spikes? We have marketing flash sales with sudden 3x traffic for 10 minutes.
[00:03:05] Jin (SE): We support autoscaling and burst buffers; Dedicated can be configured with reserved pools plus burst capacity. There's also model fallback policies — when capacity hits limits we can fallback to a cheaper, faster quantized variant or a smaller model for degraded mode.
[00:03:17] Mira (CTO): For our SLA we can't silently degrade model quality without awareness. We need a canary and a rollback path and also per-request routing rules when latency exceeds thresholds.
[00:03:26] Samir (AE): That's a good point — Redwood Rollouts allow canary/A-B and automatic fallback with alerting. We'll include that in the design doc.
[00:03:33] Leah (ML Eng): Are there known noisy neighbor concerns on hosted? If another tenant runs a big token storm, do we see p95 tail latencies inflate?
[00:03:40] Jin (SE): In multi-tenant environments there is some variability. Our smart routing and throttles mitigate, but it's less deterministic than Dedicated/Private. For strict p95 SLOs we usually recommend Dedicated or Private.
[00:03:52] [00:03:52] Speaker 2: um hmm
[00:03:54] Tom (SRE): On the benchmarking side, we'd like to run a token/sec and streaming latency benchmark using our prompt set. What's the process?
[00:04:01] Jin (SE): Typical approach: 1) we take a representative prompt set (you can share via a Google Sheet or S3), 2) we run three phases: cold-start single-conn latency, steady-state concurrency (ramping to 800 concurrent), and burst (3x) for 10 minutes. We measure first-byte p95, full completion p95, tokens/sec, GPU util, and KV cache hit rate.
[00:04:19] Mira (CTO): We have an internal prompt corpus and synthetic ramp scripts — we'll share. Do you need network egress logs or anything special for VPC?
[00:04:27] Samir (AE): For Private/VPC we can set up peering and test agents inside your VPC; we capture metrics via tracing hooks and you'll get raw traces and audit logs.
[00:04:35] Leah (ML Eng): Regarding model formats — we're currently running a mix of Llama-3 variants quantized to int8. Does Redwood support int4 or group quantization?
[00:04:43] Jin (SE): Yes, we support int8 and some int4 paths; compatibility depends on the kernel backend and model. Our optimize tooling will recommend quantization vs batch settings based on your token distributions.
[00:04:52] Tom (SRE): For cost modeling, how do you account for streaming token-by-token billing vs batch generation?
[00:04:58] Samir (AE): Pricing differs by deployment: Hosted is usage-based per-token + model tier; Dedicated has reserved capacity pricing plus overage; Private is a licensing model. Streaming doesn't change token cost but it affects how you optimize (e.g., you may want smaller models for high token-per-session workloads). We'll send an example cost model spreadsheet.
[00:05:12] Jin (SE): For p95 guarantees, Dedicated SLA can include latency SLOs for pinned capacity. Hosted SLAs focus on availability and throughput levels.
[00:05:20] Mira (CTO): What telemetry will we see in the console during a load test?
[00:05:24] Jin (SE): You'll see per-route p50/p95/p99, token rates, GPU utilization, batching histograms, KV cache hit rate, and traces to drill into individual requests. We can also stream logs to your SIEM.
[00:05:34] [00:05:34] Speaker 1: (laughs)
[00:05:36] Tom (SRE): On the security checklist — SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, SOC2, encryption at rest with BYOK — are there any gaps?
[00:05:43] Samir (AE): We support SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs. SOC2 is available for enterprise customers. BYOK/KMS for Dedicated and Private, and hosted has options for enterprise BYOK via HSM integrations. We'll share the security pack link.
[00:05:56] Mira (CTO): Good. For the benchmark we want side-by-side tests: your hosted at our sim traffic, and a dedicated small pool (2–4 GPUs) with same model to compare p95. Timeframe?
[00:06:06] Jin (SE): We can run hosted tests quickly; dedicated pool needs provisioning but we can spin a short-term trial cluster. Timeline: if you share prompt set and a timeslot, we can run hosted tests within 48 hours, dedicated within 5 business days.
[00:06:18] Leah (ML Eng): Any tooling you recommend for generating realistic concurrency? We'll use locust but open to suggestions.
[00:06:23] Jin (SE): Locust is fine. We also provide a benchmark harness script that simulates streaming clients and measures first-byte timing. We'll attach it.
[00:06:31] Tom (SRE): About model fallback — how do you handle quality regression alerts when a fallback is used?
[00:06:36] Samir (AE): Our Quality monitors link to eval suites. If a fallback is enabled we can tie alerts to prompt sets and flag drop in evaluation scores and notify owners in Slack/email.
[00:06:46] Mira (CTO): Ok let's summarize next steps.
[00:06:50] Samir (AE): Action items: 1) Silverpine to share prompt corpus and synthetic traffic scripts (Leah) — due 2027-04-08. 2) Redwood to run hosted baseline benchmarks and share results — target 2027-04-08. 3) Redwood to provision a short-term Dedicated trial and run the same tests — target 2027-04-13. 4) Samir to send security pack and pricing spreadsheet — due 2027-04-07.
[00:07:10] Leah (ML Eng): Sounds good. Also please capture first-byte p95 and 99 for streaming and include GPU util per step.
[00:07:16] Jin (SE): Will do. We'll include KV cache hit-rate and batching histograms.
[00:07:21] Tom (SRE): One more question — can we run a private/VPC pilot later if Dedicated meets latency but we need stricter data residency?
[00:07:27] Samir (AE): Absolutely, customers often start hosted -> dedicated -> private as they lock down controls.
[00:07:33] Mira (CTO): Great thanks. That covers it.
[00:07:36] Samir (AE): Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the benchmark plan and dates.
[00:07:40] [00:07:40] End of recording (note: transcript may contain transcription errors, some speaker labels are generic).
